safety_lead_time.comparison_action: REDUCE from SAP 2.5 days to recommended 2.1 days

narrative: Material PL1__M14F8FC2 exhibits moderate continuous demand averaging ~799 units/day with low-to-moderate variability (CV=0.33) and a slight declining trend. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.45, range 0.31-6.43 days), which drives 84% of safety stock requirements. An (r,Q) policy with EOQ-derived order quantity, capped by storage capacity, provides the optimal balance between ordering frequency and holding cost while meeting the 95% service level target. The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock and is exposed to frequent stockouts.
warnings: Storage capacity is binding: EOQ=10226 capped to 9709 to satisfy max_storage_units=11396 with SS=1687.
Lead time highly unstable (CV=0.45). Safety stock is predominantly driven by lead time variance (84%).
Max inventory post-replenishment = 11396 units, utilizing 99.99% of storage capacity. No headroom for safety stock increases without storage expansion.
9 demand outliers detected and winsorized at P1/P99 bounds.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) continuous-review reorder-point with fixed EOQ order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is near-continuous with moderate CV (0.33), making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy optimal. EOQ minimises total ordering plus holding cost; safety stock at the reorder point ensures 95% cycle service level despite high lead time variability.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity cap reduces order quantity from unconstrained EOQ of 10226 to 9709 units, increasing annual ordering frequency by ~5% and ordering cost proportionally. At 100% capacity utilisation post-replenishment, any demand upside or SS increase would require storage expansion.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none - policy is capacity-feasible; however storage headroom is fully exhausted and should be flagged for capacity planning review
